I don't think this news is getting the attention it deserves. The re-opening, after 12 years, of this section of the historic Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline gives Baghdad not only more options to export, but also could fast-track the redevelopment of the massive Kirkuk oilfield (where BP and ConocoPhillips are working)

Iraq says it has re-started oil exports via its historic Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline after a 12-year hiatus (Ceyhan is a Turkish port in the Mediterranean Sea).

The line inside Iraqi territory was sabotaged in 2014. At the time, the Kurdistan regional government built a second line from its territory, linking to the original pipeline at the Iraq-Turkish border (in Faysh Khabur), allowing KRG oil exports while the rest of the line inside Iraqi territory remained out of service. 

Baghdad said the now re-activated Kirkuk-to-the Turkish border portion of the pipeline would pump at 120,000 b/d initially, with aim of raising that to 500,000 b/d at an undetermined future date.

#Commodities

#CrudeOil: Brent trades 1% lower at USD 92.10 per barrel on the January contract, with traders shrugging off renewed tensions in the Persian Gulf to focus on the prospect of an emerging supply surplus. Both the IEA and Goldman Sachs have highlighted growing oversupply risks, with the latter projecting a surplus of around 2 million barrels per day in 2027 and an average Brent price of USD 88 next year. Ahead of today's EIA inventory report, the API reported a 5.3-million-barrel build in US crude stocks, alongside rising fuel inventories. Meanwhile, gasoil (diesel) has fallen to a three-month low near USD 160 per barrel, signalling easing tightness in refined products.

Precious metals: Investor confidence continues to deteriorate as momentum selling by leveraged funds extends the correction across precious metals. #Gold has fallen 1.9% to a fresh 14-month low at USD 3,780, while #silver is approaching USD 45, pushing the gold-to-silver ratio (XAUXAG) to a one-year high. The selloff is being driven by hawkish Fed commentary pointing to the need for several additional rate hikes before spring to contain stubborn inflation, alongside continued dollar strength and real yields at multi-decade highs. One relative bright spot remains ETF demand, which has shown a modest pickup during the latest price slump, suggesting some longer-term investors continue to see value despite the deteriorating technical outlook.

#Copper: The correction deepens, with December HG futures slumping 2.8% to a seven-month low of USD 5.815 per pound. A stronger dollar, Fed rate hike focus, turmoil in the AI sector and a subdued Chinese demand outlook continue to weigh on sentiment. Adding to the uncertainty is the prospect of Washington deciding against copper import tariffs, potentially triggering a reversal of the substantial buildup in US inventories over the past year.
